maker: Brad Cox and Tom Love, then NeXT and Apple
summary: C with Smalltalk-style messages, created by Brad Cox and Tom Love. NeXT made it the language of its system, and through NeXT it became the language of Mac OS X and the first iPhone apps, until Swift took over.

icon.licence: MIT (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

image.alt: A NeXTcube computer, whose software was written in Objective-C
image.credit: Michael Hicks from Saint Paul, MN, USA

events.note: Brad Cox and Tom Love create Objective-C at their company, Productivity Products International.

events.label: NeXT
events.note: NeXT licenses Objective-C and builds its operating system on it.

image.caption: NeXT licensed Objective-C for its NeXTSTEP system.

events.label: Apple
events.note: Apple buys NeXT, and Objective-C becomes the language of Mac OS X.

events.label: Objective-C 2.0
events.note: Ships with Mac OS X 10.5, adding garbage collection and properties.

events.label: Swift arrives
events.note: Apple introduces Swift, which gradually replaces Objective-C.

note: Still supported by Apple, but new Apple code is written in Swift.
